subject: Paralycopodites opposite-row compact lateral-branch lycopsid
factual_scope: Genus-level living reconstruction, not exact fossil individual. Lateral row position and determinate branching use DiMichele and Bateman2020 primary text. Cone and leaf dimensions are illustrative choices near described specimens, not universal fossil ranges. Anatomy pixels are Seward1910 fig186A/B under a historical name linked to Paralycopodites by DiMichele1980; they do not directly demonstrate whole architecture. Exact height, counts, colors and complete outline are artistic.
identifying_features: One columnar main trunk ending in a limited two-leader fork; ten compact lateral systems in two opposite vertical rows on the main trunk, and four continuing those rows on crown axes. Not helical or radial branch whorls.

Each of fourteen lateral systems forms four unequal terminal axes on a broadly planar anisotomous scaffold; fifty-six slender terminal strobili, small persistent narrow microphylls on twigs and trunk.
Four subdued basal rhizomorph beginnings. No flowers, fruit, spherical cones, terminal-only Lepidodendron crown, coarse diamond bark armor or invented expansive modern tree roots.

concept_decisions: Actual generated image inspected. Keep paired opposite-row compact side systems and limited crown fork. Reduce overlarge cones to approximately 55mm length in metre-scale geometry; retain narrow cigars not balls. Reject coarse diamond bark armor and woody modern spreading roots; show small persistent microphyll cues and four short subdued basal rhizomorph beginnings. Make trunk continuous and branch systems planar but occupy true depth.
